### W02 — A useful criterion for recognizing a completed check

**File / scan / locus:** P57, 57:92–94; CT, 47:7, top-degree identity, and 47:8, unit reduction.  
**Kind:** own idea.  
**Bears on:** WG2 §2.4 #4 — planning question, unchecked.  
**Search:** tau | Lambda | identité | compatibilité | exterior

**Confidence: high for this diagnostic criterion, because it follows from the displayed comparison map:** after the reduction to an algebraically closed field, a completed witness must calculate the maps induced by \(\mathbf Le^*(\mathbf Rp_*W)\to\mathbf Le^*e_*\tau[-n]\), not merely identify their source and target dimensions. Writing \(T=\operatorname{Lie}(B^*)\), the degree-\(i\) comparison is between \(\Lambda^iT\) and \(\Lambda^{n-i}T^\vee\otimes\det T\), and the particular induced maps must be isomorphisms compatible with the top-degree identity. CN F8, at CT 47:7–8, supplies the abstract exterior-power comparison but not that calculation; P57 57:94's mixed Künneth class is a possible neighbouring input, not a substitute. This refines the search criterion without claiming a new proof or a global splitting.

### A01 — The initial obstruction class has a restricted hypothesis

**File / scan / locus:** P57, 57:89, opening and Leray display.  
**Kind:** unproved claim.

**Search:** obstruction | connexion | Im | Ker | omega

The calculation begins by assuming that the Picard section “provient d'un faisceau inversible” and identifies an \(H^1(S,\omega_{X/S})\) class with a kernel in the Leray edge sequence. To use it for an arbitrary Picard-sheaf section, one must account for local representatives and descent, and fix the topology and the identification of the differential pushforward used in the Leray sequence. ### A08 — Oda gives a precise finite-group-scheme comparison

**File / scan / locus:** P57, 57:91–94; CT, 54:3 and 54:7 final question; Oda, printed p.131/PDF p.70, Corollary 5.11.  
**Kind:** unpursued implication.  
**Bears on:** WG2 §1.1 #3 — planning question, unchecked; SC D04 and D07 — first-pass leads.  
**Search:** Dieudonné | de Rham | extension | p^A | Corollary 5.11

CT 54:7 asks whether “Cette extension” can be recovered from \(p^A\), and P57 57:91–94 supplies an adjacent geometric extension construction. Oda's Corollary 5.11, over a perfect field of characteristic \(p>0\), gives a canonical Dieudonné-module isomorphism \(M(A[p])\simeq H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(A)\) and identifies the Hodge subspace through the Frobenius/Verschiebung data. This confirms the precise printed comparison already flagged by SC D04 at 57:285–287, 291–292, but identifying CT's particular restricted-Lie extension still requires checking its maps, twists, duality conventions and restricted \(p\)-operation. Neither abstract geometric \(p\)-torsion points nor an unqualified Tate module is being substituted for the full finite group scheme.

For a smooth proper \(X\) with a rational point over a perfect characteristic-\(p\) field, Oda 5.12 gives an injection from the relevant dual Picard \(p\)-torsion Dieudonné module into \(H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(X)\), with image \(\bigcap_n\ker(d\circ V^n)\). The following diagram retains a semilinear twist and exact columns; it supplies neither a canonical splitting of the Hodge sequence nor a relative-flatness theorem over an arbitrary base. This sharpens the use of CT 54:3, 5–7 and SC D05/D07/D08, citing 57:287–288, 294, 297 and 309–311, in reading the current extension and cohomological-flatness hypotheses. Oda's remark that 5.11 was conjectured in his reference [15] points to Grothendieck's 1966 de Rham paper, not an identification of these undated manuscript leaves.

MPL_57_089-132#26.text:
### B07 — Original-field classes are not the whole geometric generic fibre

**File / scan / locus:** P57, 57:99, theorem arrow and Corollary 1; 100, “sans partie fixe”.  
**Kind:** own idea.  
**Bears on:** Hua 57-generic-hyperplane-h1-injective — conjecture/unsearched intake status.  
**Search:** H^1 | K | partie fixe | infinitésimal | injectif

**Confidence: high, because the source and target fields are explicit:** the asserted source is \(H^1(X,G)\), not \(H^1(X_{\bar K},G_{\bar K})\), so the assertion tests torsors defined over \(k\). Even for vector spaces, \(k^2\to k(t)\), \((a,b)\mapsto a+tb\), is injective, whereas its \(k(t)\)-linear extension has the nonzero kernel generated by \((-t,1)\). H pp.98–99/scans 99–100 retains the original-field source, while the current manuscript additionally supplies “sans partie fixe,” consistent with this distinction. Thus this statement alone does not eliminate moving geometric tangent directions or prove a zero scheme-theoretic Picard kernel.

H pp.98–99/scans 99–100 and CT 44:4 are related restriction comparators, but the present source itself cancels “\(\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Pic}(Y_{\bar K})\) est injectif” and excludes \(\mathrm G_m\) from the reduction. [Grothendieck, FGA V, exposé 232](https://www.numdam.org/article/SB_1961-1962__7__143_0.pdf), Theorem 3.1, proves Picard-scheme existence for projective flat morphisms of locally noetherian schemes with geometrically integral fibres. It does not verify the more general edited parameter construction on scans 126–128 or date those leaves.

**File / scan / locus:** P57, 57:129 and 131, affine restriction to components.  
**Kind:** own idea.  
**Bears on:** WG2 §1.1 #3 — planning question, unchecked; RS MPL_57_271-315 C04 — first-pass lead.

**Confidence: high for this test case, because the gluing parameters are explicit:** glue two copies of \(\mathbf P^1\) along two pairs of distinct points over an algebraically closed field, obtaining a proper nodal curve. A line bundle trivial on each component is specified by two nonzero gluing scalars modulo simultaneous rescaling, giving kernel \(k^\times\) on \(k\)-points; the same calculation in families identifies the kernel of Picard functors with \(\mathbf G_m\). SC C04/I03 at 57:304–305 isolates the same units-to-Picard mechanism, and H pp.128, 130/scans 129, 131 predicts an affine kernel, consistent with this example. It is a useful control case for the proposition and for CR's generalized-Jacobian bridge B11, with no assertion about arithmetic finite generation or historical novelty.

MPL_58_020-067#5.text:
### N04. Connected generic fibre alone does not give the special-fibre claim

**File/scan:** 58:23, Theorem 2, hypotheses (a)–(b). **Kind:** own idea, refining a context diagnosis. **Context search:** N04; H, “Les fibres spéciales d'un morphisme propre,” their pp. 22–26, explicitly adds “géométriquement” to the generic-fibre condition. **RS:** R0. **Confidence:** high for the example, because the fibres are computed explicitly.

M says that X₁ is “connexe en dim ≥ h,” without geometrically, and H's diagnosis can be tested while retaining the written lower bound dim X₁≥h+1: take B=Spec ℤ_(5), D=ℤ_(5)[i], and X=ℙ¹_D→B, with h=0. The base is regular and geometrically unibranch, X is integral and proper over B, its sole component dominates B, and its generic fibre ℙ¹_ℚ(i) is connected of dimension one. Since T²+1=(T−2)(T+2) over 𝔽₅, the special fibre is the disjoint union of two copies of ℙ¹_𝔽₅, so the stated conclusion fails for this literal connected-generic-fibre formulation. This product construction strengthens H's finite-cover example to meet the dimension condition; it does not establish that every other hypothesis in a repaired geometrically connected version is sufficient.

### N05. Formal equidimensionality is explicitly conjectural in the reduction

**File/scan:** 58:25, second half and margin. **Kind:** self-flagged: unverified step. **Context search:** N05; H, “Les fibres spéciales,” their p. 24, adds excellence/formal-equidimensionality discussion rather than deriving the reduction from the written assumptions. **RS:** R0.

The reduction is labelled “facile (?)” and the margin says “conjecture” beside the passage to a formally equidimensional local base. This is a real gap in the reduction as presented, even if a theorem with stronger hypotheses is available. A proof must specify an allowed alteration or base change, show that it preserves the required connectedness assertion, and justify the subsequent dimension formula; “quotient of a regular ring,” excellence, and universal catenarity are different possible inputs and should not be silently substituted for one another.

**File/scan:** 58:25 and 27, displayed dimension equality and first paragraph; 58:26 is intervening reused typescript. **Kind:** reading question / unproved claim. **Context search:** N06; H, “Les fibres spéciales,” their pp. 24–26, deliberately reindexes the dimension count. **RS:** R0.

The calculation following “D'où” carries K+1=(n+h)+1 and then K−n=k|h in M, while the preceding lemma involves a local or completed spectrum and its punctured version in uncertain notation. Any future proof should state separately the dimension of the local scheme, that of its punctured spectrum, and the number of equations used, before deciding whether an off-by-one error is mathematical or palaeographical.

MPL_58_020-067#61.text:
### N60. A precise conditional interpretation of the genus identity

**File/scan:** 58:66, lower formulas and nodal drawings. **Kind:** own idea, clarifying a context interpretation. **Context search:** N60; H, “Brouillons,” their p. 65, interprets the same identity as arithmetic genus; RS cites only a lead to cote 43's local Rosenlicht theory. **RS:** MPL_43_094-142 A01, first-pass research lead, not the full earlier file. **Confidence:** high for the stated normalization calculation; medium for identifying every handwritten symbol with it.

For a connected reduced proper curve over an algebraically closed field with normalization $\pi:\coprod C_i\to C$, the normalization exact sequence gives $1-p_a(C)=\sum_i(1-g(C_i))-\operatorname{length}(\pi_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde C}/\mathcal O_C)$. Thus the written g=1+∑g_i+∑n_s−ν is compatible with n_s=δ_s and ν the number of normalized components, under those assumptions. For nodes, δ_s=1 and this becomes g=∑g_i+b₁ of the connected dual graph; general singularities have additional δ-contributions not determined by that graph. This explains a possible link to A01, but the source does not define n_s, and the displayed k[x,y,z]/(xy) is a surface ring rather than, by itself, a complete curve example.

MPL_58_020-067#65.text:
### N64. The final line-bundle question has a seminormal sufficient condition

**File/scan:** 58:67, final paragraph and margin. **Kind:** self-flagged question / own idea. **Context search:** N64; H, “Brouillons,” their p. 66, proposes seminormality in place of local factoriality. **RS:** R0. **Confidence:** high for the sufficient condition and descent argument; no claim of necessity for a particular bundle.

“Faudrait supposer X localement factoriel??” accompanies an isomorphism marked “(?)”, and the proof stops after establishing injectivity using the zero section. If X is reduced, seminormal, and of finite type over k, Traverso's polynomial Picard theorem applies on affine trivializations of the total line bundle, giving local pullbacks of the restriction to the zero section (Traverso, 1970, Theorem 3.6). Choose those identifications to be the identity on that section; their overlaps then agree because a polynomial unit over a reduced ring has no positive-degree coefficients, so they glue and prove surjectivity. This verifies H's sufficient-condition proposal, explains why local factoriality is stronger than needed, and leaves the handwritten unfinished proof intact.

### N79. The off-Y′ Hom assertion is a checked consequence of Raynaud's comparison

**File/scan:** 58:46–48, final Hom/section assertion. **Kind:** own idea: literature deduction, independently checked in this run. **Context search:** N79; H, “Une forme locale,” their pp. 45–47; Hua findings register L58; the supplied context contains no such Raynaud derivation. **RS:** L58, supplied as candidate; assessment here: the precise Hom claim below follows from a published comparison, without settling effectivity. **Confidence:** high under the explicitly stated completeness and closed-point conventions.

Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a noetherian local quotient of a regular noetherian ring, separated and complete for $(t)$, with $t\in\mathfrak m$, $P=\operatorname{Spec}A-\{\mathfrak m\}$, $D=V(t)\cap P$, and let G be coherent with depth at least two at every point **closed in P** and outside D; then $\operatorname{Hom}_P(F,G)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\widehat P}(\widehat F,\widehat G)$ is an isomorphism for every coherent F. The elementary closure-dimension and depth-localisation argument in `records/local_hom_inference.md` verifies the n=2 hypotheses of Raynaud (1974, I.1.1 and I.1.3, pp. 31–32), applied to $\mathcal Hom(F,G)$. In the only nontrivial intermediate case, a two-dimensional local domain admits a height-one specialization avoiding t, and depth at that specialization forces depth at least one at its generic point (The Stacks Project Authors, 2026, Tag 0FCC). This is our checked literature inference supporting Hua's target-only refinement, not a statement that the manuscript's dévissage is complete or that its revised essential image and algebraisation assertions follow.

MPL_60_002-035#1.text:
### F01 — Characteristic polynomials and exterior traces

**Witness:** 60/003, opening display; **kind:** unproved claim; **quote:** “on pose”. **Context query:** `characteristic polynomial|car. pol.|endomorphisme`; **comparison:** CT 16/048 uses rational characteristic coefficients to recover an inverse, whereas this page supplies the underlying linear determinant identity. **RS:** bears on WG2 §2.4 #3 and WG2 §6. #9 only at the linear-algebraic level.

The equality \(\det(1-ft)=\sum_i(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(\Lambda^if)t^i\) requires no semisimplicity: after extension to an algebraic closure, triangularize f and compare elementary symmetric functions of its diagonal entries. Zero eigenvalues explain why the roots are inverses only of nonzero eigenvalues, a restriction the manuscript states explicitly. This identity does not supply the rationality of characteristic coefficients for algebraic correspondences over a rational coefficient field in CT 16/048.

MPL_60_002-035#2.text:
### F02 — Symmetric powers and exact-sequence multiplicativity

**Witness:** 60/003, middle displays; **kind:** unproved claim; **quote:** “suite exacte … produit des polynômes”. **Context query:** `groupe de Grothendieck|suite exacte|rang virtuel`; **comparison:** CT 16/035 defines a split Grothendieck group in a reused Karoubi typescript, while CT 47/008 uses a virtual rank in a different derived setting. **RS:** MPL_15_195-228+18_002-017 R01 is a relevant first-pass warning about treating reused text as motivic evidence; no exact RS theorem settles this item.

For an f-stable short exact sequence, an adapted basis makes f block triangular, so characteristic polynomials multiply and their reciprocals do as well. The symmetric-power trace identity follows by expanding the product of geometric series, including in positive characteristic; it does not require division by factorials. The word “additif” therefore concerns addition in a Grothendieck group mapping to ordinary multiplication of series, not addition of rational functions.

MPL_60_002-035#3.text:
### F03 — The written product is the rational Witt construction

**Witness:** 60/003 and 005; **kind:** unpursued implication; **quote:** “(1−at)*(1−bt)=1−abt”. **Context query:** `Grothendieck|produit tensoriel|lambda|sigma`; **comparison:** CT 16/035 gives a separate K-group construction and CT 47/009 uses Chern operations, but neither supplied passage identifies this rational-function multiplication. **RS:** WG2 §2.4 #3, with no construction of motives inferred.

The elementary-factor rule identifies the polynomial/quotient part with the rational Witt ring, with ordinary series multiplication serving as addition and tensor product supplying the second multiplication. Blumberg et al. (2013, introduction and §6; published 2016) use precisely this rule and describe the rational subring; that is a later mathematical comparison, not a dating or priority claim about the present undated pages. The finite-polynomial restriction on scan 007 is consequently structural, not merely a convergence warning.

MPL_60_002-035#4.text:
### F04 — Reciprocal L-functions change the additive sign convention

**Witness:** 60/005, first and last displays; **kind:** reading question; **quote:** “L … = 1/(L*L)”. **Context query:** `sigma|lambda|produit|K^`; **comparison:** CT 47/009 has formal Chern powers but no matching tensor-L convention. **RS:** no exact matching entry; related only to WG2 §2.4 #3.

Replacing P by \(L=P^{-1}\) is additive negation in the Witt convention, which explains why tensor and exterior/symmetric formulas acquire inversions. The next multi-factor expression is written with a product sign, so it should be checked as a Witt product before being used as ordinary multiplication: for two one-dimensional endomorphisms a,b, \(L_{a\otimes b}=1/(1-abt)\), whereas the ordinary reciprocal of \(L_aL_b\) is \((1-at)(1-bt)\). This is a notes-only interpretation question; no star has been inserted into the frozen display.

MPL_60_002-035#5.text:
### F05 — The same-page cancelled λ identity is not a second theorem

**Witness:** 60/005, crossed-out product and final brace; **kind:** withdrawn in the same text; **quote:** the deleted product ending “−1”. **Context query:** `lambda|sigma|classes de Chern`; **comparison:** CT 47/009 also experiments with formal operations, but has no identical cancellation. **RS:** no exact matching entry.

The usable proof obligation is to reconstruct those final formulas with the manuscript's additive and multiplicative conventions fixed; the crossed-out expression cannot be cited as a live claim. This also explains why a conventional λ-ring identity should not be used to repair the cancelled ink.

MPL_60_002-035#6.text:
### F06 — Contragrédient reciprocity has a rational-function domain

**Witness:** 60/007, final paragraph; **kind:** unpursued implication; **quote:** “produits … finis de polynômes”. **Context query:** `ration|polynôme|automorphisme`; **comparison:** CT 16/048 uses Cayley–Hamilton for inverses, a related finite algebraic calculation but not a formal-series substitution theorem. **RS:** WG2 §6. #9 is background only.

The warning is justified because an arbitrary series in \(k[[t]]\) cannot generally be evaluated at \(t^{-1}\) inside that ring. For an automorphism of rank r, the elementary identity is \(P_{(f^{-1})^\vee}(t)=(-t)^r\det(f)^{-1}P_f(t^{-1})\), and quotients of finite polynomials with invertible relevant coefficients allow the same rational manipulation. The uncertain minus sign in one intermediate argument remains a reading question, not a correction licensed by the boxed identity.

MPL_60_002-035#7.text:
### F07 — Epsilon changes meaning within the packet

**Witness:** 60/007, boxed exponent; 021/027, virtual ranks; **kind:** reading question; **quote:** “ε(Rf_!(E))”. **Context query:** `rang virtuel|varepsilon|epsilon`; **comparison:** CT 47/008 explicitly glosses ε as virtual rank, while cote 60 also uses ε(E) for a normalized determinant. **RS:** MPL_15_195-228+18_002-017 M03 is a first-pass reminder that similarly named gradings and characters require definitions.

MPL_60_002-035#8.text:
### F08 — Purity alone does not force determinant sign ±1

**Witness:** 60/009, determinant paragraph; **kind:** unproved claim; **quote:** “s'il s'agit d'un motif”. **Context query:** `ration|Weil|characteristic polynomial`; **comparison:** CT 16/048 explicitly adds rational characteristic coefficients and CT 16/050 proposes deriving Weil from its conjectural inputs. **RS:** WG2 §2.3 #7; MPL_14_002-044 M29 and MPL_14_087-132 M09 remain first-pass distinctions, not proofs of realization claims.

Absolute values alone give an absolute value for the determinant, not a real sign: a rank-one finite-order character with Frobenius a primitive cube root of unity is pure of weight zero but has determinant different from ±1 over a coefficient field containing that root. Rationality or a suitable selfduality/polarization is therefore a substantive extra input in the motivic clause. The opening replacement of “motif” by “Q_l-faisceau” does not erase the later explicit restriction back to a motive.

MPL_60_002-035#9.text:
### F09 — Why the odd-weight dimension must be even under rationality

**Witness:** 60/009 and 023; **kind:** unproved claim; **quote:** “tjrs entier”. **Context query:** `ration|poids|Weil`; **comparison:** adds a numerical consequence to CT 16/048–050, where rationality and the Weil programme are separate inputs. **RS:** WG2 §2.4 #3 and WG2 §2.3 #7.

If the determinant is rational and equals \(\pm p^{n\rho/2}\) with p prime, then odd nρ would make its square-root factor irrational, proving nρ even. Without that rationality input, a one-dimensional \(\mathbf Q_\ell\)-representation with Frobenius \(\sqrt p\), when \(\sqrt p\in\mathbf Q_\ell\), is a pure odd-weight counterexample to the unrestricted statement. This argument uses p prime as written and should not be transferred unchanged to a square prime-power base field.

MPL_60_002-035#10.text:
### F10 — Selfduality is a hypothesis on the coefficient object

**Witness:** 60/009, “par Lefschetz”; 013 and 017; **kind:** unproved claim; **quote:** “check E ≃ E(ρ)”. **Context query:** `motive-theoretically|dual|Lefschetz`; **comparison:** CT 16/048 discusses motive-theoretic identification with a dual while explicitly dropping a twist; CT 16/049 needs additional inputs for algebraic splittings. **RS:** WG2 §2.4 #3; MPL_14_087-132 M01 and M09, both first-pass leads.

A nondegenerate pairing of the appropriate weight yields this isomorphism, but an arbitrary pure lisse sheaf need not possess one. The manuscript's later “si on admet que” and its favorable-case restriction are therefore material, not redundant qualifications. These pages use a motivic duality package; they do not construct it from the Lefschetz correspondence rings of cote 16.

MPL_60_002-035#11.text:
### F11 — A Tate twist supplies the variable change

**Witness:** 60/009, final equality; **kind:** unpursued implication; **quote:** “L_checkE(t)=L_E(t/p^ρ)”. **Context query:** `twist|Tate|dual`; **comparison:** CT 16/048 explicitly suppresses a twist, while CT 47/004–005 tracks shifts in another functorial calculation. **RS:** MPL_15_195-228+18_002-017 P09 is an earlier first-pass twist-convention question.

Under the convention stated above, tensoring by \(\mathbf Q_\ell(\rho)\) scales every Frobenius eigenvalue by \(p^{-\rho}\), hence gives the displayed substitution directly. The positive \(\mathbf Q_\ell(n)\) written later in scan 015's pairing should be kept as a separate convention/reading question rather than used to reverse this explicit calculation. Twists and cohomological shifts have different effects on an L-function and must be tracked separately.

**Witness:** 60/011, amended hypothesis; 019–021; **kind:** withdrawn in the same text; **quote:** deleted “compactifiable”, inserted “propre”. **Context query:** `propre|compact|dualit`; **comparison:** CT 47/004–005 and CN F20 concern proper derived operations, not the present nonproper boundary correction. **RS:** no exact matching entry; WG2 §2.4 #3 is thematic.

The page narrows its first global-duality calculation to proper X, then scans 019–021 restore a compactifiable nonproper setting by keeping \(Rf_!\) and \(Rf_*\) distinct. The boundary L-factor is the added content that makes this later return substantive. Quoting the first formula with the struck-out broader hypothesis would suppress the manuscript's own correction.


## B. Proper duality, parity, and normalization

MPL_60_002-035#13.text:
### F13 — Derived determinant reciprocity follows degree by degree

**Witness:** 60/011, equation (1); **kind:** unproved claim; **quote:** “par le th. de dualité globale”. **Context query:** `dualit|complexe|rang virtuel`; **comparison:** CT 47/004–005 explicitly distinguishes derived shifts from the class-level formula, but contains no corresponding L-function equation. **RS:** MPL_15_195-228+18_002-017 M03/P09 are first-pass convention leads; no exact settled entry applies.

For a finite-dimensional Frobenius complex V, apply the inverse-eigenvalue identity of F06 in each degree and take alternating products to obtain \(L_{DV}(t)=(-t)^{-\chi(V)}\delta(V)L_V(t^{-1})\). Proper duality identifies \(D Rf_*E\) with \(Rf_*DE\), giving the manuscript's formula without a purity or semisimplicity assumption. Deligne (1973, §§10.3.4–10.5) supplies a later primary formulation of this determinant-and-duality calculation.

**Witness:** 60/013, opening calculation; **kind:** unproved claim; **quote:** “comme b_i=b_{2n-i}”. **Context query:** `dual|Betti|Lefschetz`; **comparison:** CT 16/014–018 supplies alternating/Lefschetz structures and CT 16/048 explicitly asks for motivic duality; the present page computes a determinant consequence. **RS:** WG2 §6. #9; MPL_14_087-132 M05 is a first-pass grading warning.

Given that equality, replacing i by \(2n-i\) in the alternating sum proves \(\sum_i(-1)^i i b_i=n\chi(E)\), hence the exponent \((n+\rho)\chi(E)/2\). The algebraic simplification is sound once that coefficient-level hypothesis is supplied.

**Witness:** 60/013, small insertion; **kind:** self-flagged / reading question; **quote:** “si on admet que”; “il suffit … sur le corps des fonctions”. **Context query:** `corps des fonctions|générique|normal|isomorph`; **comparison:** CT 16/049 discusses algebraicity of inverses and splittings, not extension of lisse-sheaf morphisms from a generic point. **RS:** no exact matching entry; the category-construction question WG2 §2.4 #3 remains separate.

MPL_60_002-035#17.text:
### F17 — Even shifts are invisible to L but visible to duality

**Witness:** 60/013 and 019, explicit [2n]; 025 and 033, omitted even shifts; **kind:** unpursued implication; **quote:** “shift”. **Context query:** `shift|degré|decal|décal|[-n]`; **comparison:** CT 47/005 retains a derived shift while CT 47/008 computes its parity effect; cote 60 supplies another instance of the same distinction. **RS:** MPL_15_195-228+18_002-017 M03/P09/P14, all first-pass leads.

For lisse E on a smooth n-dimensional X, the full formula is \(D_XE=E^\vee(n)[2n]\), so the selfdual specialization gives \(E(n+\rho)[2n]\). An even shift leaves \(\chi,\delta,L\) unchanged, whereas an odd shift changes the virtual sign and inverts \(\delta,L\). Consequently the missing [2n] on 025 and [2] on 033 can be harmless in the subsequent L-function calculation without being correct as literal derived-object identities.

**Witness:** 60/015, final three displays; **kind:** unproved claim; **quote:** “Pour la raison analogue” (uncertain reading). **Context query:** `altern|dual|signe|discrimin`; **comparison:** CT 16/014 and 025 concern nondegenerate pairings; this page adds a Frobenius-determinant application. **RS:** MPL_14_002-044 A36 is a first-pass autoduality lead, not a checked proof of this formula.

MPL_60_002-035#21.text:
### F21 — Odd-weight positivity uses an alternating polarization

**Witness:** 60/017, opening paragraph; 023, odd-index sign; **kind:** unproved claim; **quote:** “une forme alternée non dégénérée”. **Context query:** `forme alternée|symplect|polar|Lefschetz`; **comparison:** CT 16/014 begins with precisely an alternating nondegenerate form, while 16/048–050 treats additional motivic inputs as conjectural. **RS:** WG2 §2.4 #3 and WG2 §6. #9.

If a 2m-dimensional space carries a nondegenerate alternating form and F multiplies that form by a positive scalar c, then \(\det F=c^m\); after normalization its determinant is +1. Thus the stated alternating-form hypothesis proves the sign conclusion and the even-dimension assertion, including without semisimplicity of F. Pure weight or selfduality without the required symmetry type does not suffice, as F22 tests.

MPL_60_002-035#22.text:
### F22 — A symmetric odd-weight selfduality is a scope counterexample

**Witness:** 60/017 and 023; **kind:** own idea; **quote:** “+1 si i est impair”. **Confidence:** high; both the pairing and determinant are verified by 2×2 matrix multiplication. **Context query:** `semi-simple|polar|symétrique|alternée`; **comparison:** CT 16/048–050 separates duality, positivity and semisimplicity; this example makes that separation concrete. **RS:** bears on first-pass MPL_14_002-044 M29a and MPL_14_087-132 M09 only as a separate local-system scope test.

On \(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_p\), let \(F=\begin{pmatrix}0&p\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\) and \(B=\operatorname{diag}(1,p)\), with \(\ell\ne p\). Then \(F^tBF=pB\), so \(E^\vee\simeq E(1)\), and the rational characteristic polynomial \(x^2-p\) gives pure weight 1, but \(\det F=-p\) and \(\varepsilon'=\varepsilon=-1\). This symmetric pairing therefore disproves extending the odd-weight positive-sign assertion to all rational, pure, selfdual sheaves; it does not contradict a polarized motivic assertion with alternating symmetry.

MPL_60_002-035#23.text:
### F23 — Eigenvalues ±1 require normalized Frobenius

**Witness:** 60/017, even-weight paragraph; **kind:** reading question; **quote:** deleted “dimension”, inserted “multiplicité”; “valeur propre 1 (−1)”. **Context query:** `Frobenius|valeur propre|multiplicité|Weil`; **comparison:** CT 16/020 has an unfinished weighted expression but no identification of these normalized eigenvalues. **RS:** MPL_14_087-132 M05 is a first-pass warning about distinct gradings.

For \(F_0=p^{-(n+\rho)/2}F\) in the orthogonal case, reciprocal eigenvalues away from ±1 pair, so \(b_n\equiv e_1+e_{-1}\pmod2\), \(\det F_0=(-1)^{e_{-1}}\), and \(\varepsilon'=(-1)^{e_1}\). These are algebraic multiplicities, not merely dimensions of ordinary eigenspaces; the insertion “multiplicité” is mathematically significant. Deligne (1974, §2.6) states the corresponding sign using the unnormalized central eigenvalue \(p^{n/2}\) over \(\mathbf F_p\), making the normalization issue explicit in the constant-coefficient case.

MPL_60_002-035#24.text:
### F24 — Projective space detects both the normalization and central-pole issue

**Witness:** 60/015–017; **kind:** own idea; **quote:** “ε′(E)=(−1)^{e_1}”. **Confidence:** high; the cohomology of \(\mathbf P^2\) gives three explicit Frobenius eigenvalues. **Context query:** `projectif|projective|espace|Lefschetz`; **comparison:** CT 16/014–018 develops Lefschetz linear algebra, but no matching central-sign test was found. **RS:** WG2 §6. #9 is thematic only.

For \(X=\mathbf P^2\) with constant coefficients, \(\chi=3\), \(\delta=p^3\), \(q=p^2\), hence \(\varepsilon=1\), \(\varepsilon'=-1\), while raw Frobenius on \(H^2\) has eigenvalue p, not 1. Normalizing by p gives multiplicity one and the correct sign, whereas the literal raw-eigenvalue interpretation fails. Moreover \(L(t)=[(1-t)(1-pt)(1-p^2t)]^{-1}\) has a simple pole at the central point \(t=1/p\), so a negative normalized sign constrains the parity of the order of a zero **or pole**, and implies a central zero only with an additional holomorphy hypothesis.

For a compactification \(j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X\), closed complement \(i:Z\hookrightarrow\bar X\), and proper \(\bar f\), localization realizes this cone as \(R\bar f_*i_*i^*Rj_*E\). MPL_60_002-035#33.text:
### F33 — Compact and ordinary normalized determinants are reciprocal

**Witness:** 60/027, two adjacent boxed identities; **kind:** own idea / inconsistency check; **quote:** “δ(E)δ′(E)=q^{χ(E)}”. **Confidence:** high; the conclusion is an algebraic consequence of the first box and has the explicit test F34. **Context query:** `déterminant|determinant|epsilon|infin`; **comparison:** CT 16/020 concerns a different determinant-style calculation and no context formula repairs this equality. **RS:** no exact matching entry.

MPL_60_002-035#34.text:
### F34 — The affine line verifies the boundary equation and separates its normalizations

**Witness:** 60/021, 025, 027 and 029; **kind:** own idea; **quote:** “=±1 si X … propre”. **Confidence:** high; only \(H_c^2(\mathbf A^1)=\mathbf Q_\ell(-1)\) and \(H^0(\mathbf A^1)=\mathbf Q_\ell\) enter. **Context query:** `affine|compact|Frobenius|fonctionnelle`; **comparison:** no matching boundary test was found in CT/CN. **RS:** no exact matching entry.

For constant coefficients on \(\mathbf A^1/\mathbf F_p\), \(q=p,\chi=1,\delta_c=p,\delta_*=1\), so the two normalized determinants are \(\sqrt p\) and \(1/\sqrt p\). Here \(L_c=(1-pt)^{-1}\), \(L_\infty=(1-pt)/(1-t)\), \(\delta_\infty=p^{-1}\), and \(A(t)=(1-pt)/(p(1-t))\). Substitution verifies both \(L_c(1/(pt))=A(t)p(-t)L_c(t)\) and \(L_\infty(t)L_\infty(1/(pt))\delta_\infty=1\), isolating the error to the normalized-determinant equality rather than the boundary functional equation.

**Witness:** 60/027 and 031; **kind:** own idea; **quote:** “ε′(E)=±1” only for complete X. **Confidence:** high; the four cohomology groups listed in the research record give the stated products directly. **Context query:** `multiplicatif|G_m|infin|ramification`; **comparison:** CT 44's reused root-system material supplies no relevant boundary comparison. **RS:** no exact matching entry.

Its compact-support L-function is \((1-t)/(1-pt)\), while \(L_\infty=((1-pt)/(1-t))^2\), reflecting the two missing points of the projective line. Thus ε need not be a sign outside the proper case, fully consistent with the manuscript's explicit qualification.

MPL_60_002-035#43.text:
### F43 — The correction can occur where the quotient is unramified

**Witness:** 60/035, support assertion; **kind:** own idea / counterexample; **quote:** “pts de ‘ramification’ de E''_y”. **Confidence:** high; the local tame relation and invariant spaces are explicit. **Context query:** `ramification|invariant|unipotent|extension`; **comparison:** CT has no matching inertia-invariants claim, and its reused algebra ramification exercises concern a different setting. **RS:** MPL_14_002-044 M29a is a first-pass mixed-extension lead; this is an independent test, not a reproof of that result.

### Trace duals, differents, socles, and orders

#### RT15 — Generic separability must be recovered before using the trace dual

**Witness:** 60/030 exercise 1 hypotheses; 60/024 exercise 3. **Kind:** reading question / scope condition. **Context:** T; adds explicit order exercises to CT 16/052 and CN R16, both earlier leads. **Context query:** `différente|codifférente|conducteur|trace`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The displayed hypotheses of exercise 1 say only that \(L/K\) has degree \(n\), while the subsequent use of \(C^*\) as a trace-dual lattice requires a nondegenerate trace pairing. In a purely inseparable extension \(k((t))/k((t^p))\), the trace is zero and the trace complement is the whole field, not a finite lattice. The missing surrounding §5 text may supply separability; the modern comparison expressly assumes a finite generically étale algebra (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d.-e).

**Witness:** 60/024 exercise 3(a). **Kind:** unproved claim. **Context:** T, related to CT 16/052 but not stated there. **Context query:** `différente|codifférente|conducteur|trace`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The assertion “égal à \(B^*:C^*\)” identifies the conductor through trace-dual lattices, and the localized product formula uses the principal-ideal property of the semilocal normalization. Its proof needs lattice biduality and the precise ambient-field meaning of the colon operation. This adds a conductor calculation to the earlier context's proposed trace different; it does not identify the Kähler and trace differents without a comparison theorem.

#### RT17 — Different containment follows the conductor comparison

**Witness:** 60/024, exercise 3(b). **Kind:** unproved claim. **Context:** T, related to CT 16/052 nos. 2–4. **Context query:** `différente|codifférente|conducteur|trace`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The containment \(\mathfrak D_{C/A}\subset\mathfrak f_{C/B}\cap\mathfrak D_{B/A}\) is to be derived from the conductor formula and reversed inclusions under trace duality. Its proof needs the finite separable-order setting of RT15. It should not be derived from the defective symbolic-degree definition.

#### RT18 — The multiplier-ring criterion has a Gorenstein interpretation

**Witness:** 60/024 exercise 3(d); 60/022 exercise 3(e). **Kind:** unpursued implication. **Context:** T; no direct previous multiplier-ring criterion was found. **Context query:** `différente|codifférente|conducteur|trace`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The condition that \(C^*\) be invertible, together with the implication \(\mathfrak a:\mathfrak a=C\Rightarrow\mathfrak a\) invertible, is the modern Gorenstein-order condition after height-one localization. For orders in number fields, Marseglia (2019, §2) explicitly gives this equivalence and distinguishes it from the stronger Bass condition on every overorder. The note should preserve that localization and order scope, rather than asserting a theorem about arbitrary rings or identifying the present typescript's author or date from modern terminology.

#### RT19 — Irreducibility does not imply a globally simple socle quotient

**Witness:** 60/022 exercise 4(a). **Kind:** own idea, counterexample to the unrestricted statement. **Context:** S, no direct matching criterion. **Context query:** `socle|primaire|irréductible`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

Take \(C=k[x,y]\) and \(\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p=(x)\): fractional ideal quotients give \(\mathfrak q:\mathfrak q=C\) and \(\mathfrak q:\mathfrak p=C\), and the prime ideal \(\mathfrak q\) is irreducible, but \((\mathfrak q:\mathfrak p)/\mathfrak q=k[y]\) is not a simple \(C\)-module. The familiar socle criterion applies after localization at \(\mathfrak p\), or when the primary support is a maximal ideal and the quotient is artinian local. **Confidence: high**, by this explicit domain example; the written “se ramener” needs that localization step.

**Witness:** 60/022, exercise 4(a), parenthetical proof hint. **Kind:** reading question. **Context:** S; no direct earlier wording match. **Context query:** `socle|primaire|irréductible`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The parenthesis calls the socle an “\((A/\mathfrak p)\)-module” although its current ring is C. The natural comparison would use \(C/\mathfrak p\), but that is a proposed reading/printing correction in these notes only. The frozen letter is not altered.

#### RT21 — The colon equality in the semilocal proof also needs localization

**Witness:** 60/022 exercise 4(b), last parenthetical clause. **Kind:** own idea, counterexample to a displayed inference. **Context:** S and T; no matching earlier equality. **Context query:** `socle|primaire|irréductible|différente|codifférente|conducteur|trace`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

**Witness:** 60/022 exercise 4(b), main assertion. **Kind:** unpursued implication / unproved claim. **Context:** T and S. **Context query:** `différente|codifférente|conducteur|trace|socle|primaire|irréductible`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

If \(C^*=uC\), multiplication by \(u^{-1}\) gives the required isomorphism, since \(\mathfrak D_{C/A}=u^{-1}C\); the converse requires the stated minimal-generator argument at every maximal ideal. Abstract equality of lengths alone would be insufficient for this converse.

**Witness:** 60/022 exercise 4(d). **Kind:** unproved claim. **Context:** V and T, no directly matching statement. **Context query:** `puissance symbolique|pseudo.inversible|degré|déterminantiel|différente|codifférente|conducteur|trace`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

**Witness:** 60/022 exercise 5, continued on 60/020. **Kind:** unproved claim / unpursued implication. **Context:** T; no directly matching earlier degree bound. **Context query:** `différente|codifférente|conducteur|trace`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

**Witness:** 60/020 exercise 6(a)–(c). **Kind:** unproved claim. **Context:** T; adds a branch/conductor formulation to CT 16/054–056. **Context query:** `différente|codifférente|conducteur|trace`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

**Witness:** 60/020 exercise 7(a). **Kind:** unproved claim / missing scope. **Context:** M; CT 16/054 also invokes a discriminant polynomial. **Context query:** `monogène|monogene|homogènes|discriminant|polynôme`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

In a DVR setting, congruence modulo a sufficiently small ideal preserves a unit determinant, but that is a qualified comparison, not text to supply in the blank reference.

**Witness:** 60/020, exercise 7(c). **Kind:** unproved claim / context addition. **Context:** M; CT 16/052 and 054, CN R6–R7. **Context query:** `monogène|monogene|homogènes|discriminant|polynôme`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

### Fitting ideals, exterior powers, and flatness

#### RT31 — The missing start of exercise 22 matters

**Witness:** 60/032, exercise 22(c)–(e). **Kind:** reading question / scope condition. **Context:** F and P; related to CT 16/052 and 54/004–006. **Context query:** `Fitting|Filting|déterminantiel|annulateur|plat|platitude|annulateur|nilpotent`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The sheet begins with part (c), while the hypotheses and definitions in 22(a)–(b) are absent from the selected package. The splitting and freeness assertions are naturally local-ring statements; without locality, a nontrivial invertible ideal over a Dedekind domain can be free at a chosen prime and modulo that prime while failing to be globally free. This is a reason to recover the preceding draft page, not a reason to accuse the omitted hypothesis of being absent in the original exercise.

#### RT32 — The invariant-factor equivalence uses cyclic splitting

**Witness:** 60/032, exercise 22(d). **Kind:** unproved claim. **Context:** F; adds an explicit local diagonalization exercise to CT 16/052. **Context query:** `Fitting|Filting|déterminantiel|annulateur`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The proposed equivalence joins principal Fitting ideals, principal annihilators of exterior powers, and a divisibility-ordered cyclic decomposition. Splitting the cyclic summand of 22(c), as isolated in RT56, gives the indicated induction. A complete proof must retain the missing local hypotheses and distinguish the product formula for Fitting ideals from individual exterior annihilators.

#### RT33 — The freeness test can be proved over a local domain

**Witness:** 60/032, exercise 22(e). **Kind:** unproved claim with an editorial proof route. **Context:** P; differs from the flattening assertions in CT 54/004–006. **Context query:** `plat|platitude|annulateur|nilpotent`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

Assuming the omitted hypotheses make \(A\) a local domain and \(E\) finite, a basis of \(E/\mathfrak pE\) lifts to generators of \(E\) by Nakayama. Their relation module inside \(A^r\) vanishes after localization at \(\mathfrak p\), because \(E_{\mathfrak p}\) is free of the same rank; since \(A\) is a domain, it was already zero. Thus the conclusion follows in that setting, while RT31 explains why a global version needs qualification.

#### RT34 — The last divisibility comparison invokes an undefined lambda

**Witness:** 60/032, exercise 22(d). **Kind:** reading question. **Context:** F; no direct earlier wording match. **Context query:** `Fitting|Filting|déterminantiel|annulateur`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The conventional endpoint would be \(r-2\) for comparisons between successive listed factors. #### RT35 — The exterior-annihilator quotient is actually finite locally free

**Witness:** 60/032, exercise 23, first claim. **Kind:** own idea / stronger consequence. **Context:** P and F; adds a precise finite-module criterion to CT 54/004–006. **Context query:** `plat|platitude|annulateur|nilpotent|Fitting|Filting|déterminantiel|annulateur`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

With the interpretation of \(r\) in RT64, localization at any prime shows \(\operatorname{Ann}(\bigwedge^rE)=\operatorname{Fitt}_{r-1}(E)\) and \(\operatorname{Fitt}_r(E)=A\): when the local generator number is \(r\), both ideals are the relation-coefficient ideal, and when it is smaller both are the unit ideal. Consequently, for \(\mathfrak a\supset\operatorname{Ann}(\bigwedge^rE)\), the quotient \(E/\mathfrak aE\) is finite locally free of rank \(r\), by Fitting base change and the rank criterion (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d.-g, n.d.-f, n.d.-a). **Confidence: high**, by this local presentation argument; this proves more than the word “plat” on the sheet and does not require assuming finite presentation of \(E\) in advance.

#### RT36 — “Radical” must be distinguished from nilradical

**Witness:** 60/032, exercise 23, last sentence. **Kind:** reading question / own test case. **Context:** P; CT 54/004–006 explicitly discusses nilpotents, which is a different issue. **Context query:** `plat|platitude|annulateur|nilpotent`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The stated corollary is compatible with the Jacobson radical: constant fiber dimension at all maximal ideals places the top-exterior annihilator in their intersection, so RT35 applies. If “radical de \(A\)” were instead interpreted as the nilradical, the assertion would fail for \(A=k[t]_{(t)}\) and \(E=A/(t)\): there is only one maximal fiber dimension, but the nilradical is zero and \(E\) is not flat. **Confidence: high** for the counterexample; the note identifies the necessary meaning of a term rather than altering it.

#### RT37 — The explicit Fitting example checks directly

**Witness:** 60/034, exercise 10(g). **Kind:** own idea / verification. **Context:** F; adds a fully calculable example to CT 16/052 and CN R14. **Context query:** `Fitting|Filting|déterminantiel|annulateur`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The standard direct-sum and cyclic-module rules give exactly \(\operatorname{Fitt}_0(M)=\mathfrak q\), \(\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)=A\), \(\operatorname{Fitt}_0(N)=\mathfrak m^2\), and \(\operatorname{Fitt}_1(N)=\mathfrak m\) (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d.-g). **Confidence: high**, by the displayed annihilation and two-element basis; no correction of this example is indicated.

**Witness:** 60/034, exercise 11(a). **Kind:** unproved claim / unpursued implication. **Context:** F and V, no exact earlier formula. **Context query:** `Fitting|Filting|déterminantiel|annulateur|puissance symbolique|pseudo.inversible|degré|déterminantiel`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

Independence of \(c\) can be checked at every height-one DVR, where multiplying a lattice by \(c\) adds \(v(c)\) to each invariant exponent. The subtraction \((n-k)\operatorname{div}(c)\) cancels exactly that contribution, permitting negative relative exponents when \(N\) is not contained in \(M\). This signed interpretation is needed before using the next part's inequalities.

#### RT39 — Monotonicity fails for arbitrary relative lattices

**Witness:** 60/034, exercise 11(b), first assertion. **Kind:** own idea, counterexample. **Context:** F and V, no direct earlier claim. **Context query:** `Fitting|Filting|déterminantiel|annulateur|puissance symbolique|pseudo.inversible|degré|déterminantiel`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

Thus the printed \(d_0\ge d_1\) is false under the displayed hypotheses, which do not require \(N\subset M\). **Confidence: high**, from the defining formula; adding containment would remove this particular obstruction, but is not a permitted transcription change.

#### RT40 — The invariant-factor endpoint is undefined

**Witness:** 60/034, exercise 11(b), second inequality. **Kind:** reading question. **Context:** F, no direct earlier wording match. **Context query:** `Fitting|Filting|déterminantiel|annulateur`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The conventional comparison would end at \(n-1\); this is a proposed index repair only. It is separate from the genuine signed-valuation counterexample to the preceding inequality.

#### RT41 — The zeroth relative divisor is the lattice characteristic

**Witness:** 60/034, exercise 11(c). **Kind:** unproved claim. **Context:** V and F; no exact matching earlier formula. **Context query:** `puissance symbolique|pseudo.inversible|degré|déterminantiel|Fitting|Filting|déterminantiel|annulateur`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The identity \(d_0(N,M)=\chi(M,N)\) compares the sum of signed local invariant exponents with the local length-difference definition of \(\chi\). At a height-one DVR, choose a common sublattice and subtract the two colengths, which yields precisely that sum. This remains compatible with negative coefficients and does not require the false monotonicity tested in RT39.

#### RT42 — The binomial coefficient counts invariant exponents

**Witness:** 60/034, exercise 12(a). **Kind:** unproved claim with an editorial proof route. **Context:** F and V, no directly matching earlier exterior-divisor formula. **Context query:** `Fitting|Filting|déterminantiel|annulateur|puissance symbolique|pseudo.inversible|degré|déterminantiel`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

At each height-one DVR, choose bases diagonalizing \(N\subset M\); in the \(k\)-th exterior power every invariant exponent occurs in exactly \(\binom{r-1}{k-1}\) of the \(k\)-fold sums. Summing these valuations proves the displayed divisor-length identity for \(1\le k\le r\), while localization also explains “pseudo-injectif.” The proof must retain the finite torsion-free equal-rank hypotheses and should state conventions separately for exterior powers outside that range.

#### RT43 — Pseudo-null exterior torsion can be nonzero

**Witness:** 60/034, exercise 12(b). **Kind:** own idea / example. **Context:** F and V, no directly matching example. **Context query:** `Fitting|Filting|déterminantiel|annulateur|puissance symbolique|pseudo.inversible|degré|déterminantiel`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

For \(A=k[x,y]\) and the rank-one torsion-free ideal \(I=(x,y)\), a presentation with relation \((-y,x)\) gives \(\bigwedge^2 I\simeq A/(x,y)\). Thus exterior torsion need not vanish, although it vanishes at every height-one localization, exactly as “pseudo-nul” predicts. **Confidence: high**, by this explicit presentation; adjoining a free summand gives a rank-two example where \(\bigwedge^2(I\oplus A)\to\bigwedge^2(A^2)\) has this nonzero pseudo-null kernel.

### Additional separated exercise obligations

#### RT47 — The different's own multiplier ring is a separate converse

**Witness:** 60/022, exercise 3(e). **Kind:** unproved claim. **Context:** T; no direct matching criterion in CT 16/052–056. **Context query:** `différente|codifférente|conducteur|trace`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The criterion \((\mathfrak D_{C/A})_{\mathfrak p}:(\mathfrak D_{C/A})_{\mathfrak p}=C_{\mathfrak p}\) is asserted to be equivalent to invertibility of the trace dual, not merely to follow from it. The forward consequence from an invertible trace dual is straightforward because its inverse different is invertible; the converse requires an additional local-order argument about the inverse of the canonical/trace-dual ideal. The later multiplier characterization in RT18 should not be cited as though it supplies that converse for a ring not already known Gorenstein.

#### RT48 — Every normalization ideal is pseudo-invertible, not necessarily globally invertible

**Witness:** 60/030, last sentence. **Kind:** unpursued implication. **Context:** V, no direct earlier assertion. **Context query:** `puissance symbolique|pseudo.inversible|degré|déterminantiel`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

“Si \(C=B\), tout idéal \(\ne0\) de \(B\) est pseudo-inversible” only tests localizations over height-one primes of \(A\). These are semilocal one-dimensional normal domains, so their ideals are principal, while a nonzero ideal of the higher-dimensional normal ring \(B\) can still fail to be globally invertible. This distinction prevents the final sentence from being read as a claim that every normal noetherian domain is Dedekind or factorial.

#### RT49 — Normalization colength is a separate invertibility criterion

**Witness:** 60/024, exercise 2(e). **Kind:** unproved claim. **Context:** V, no direct earlier formulation. **Context query:** `puissance symbolique|pseudo.inversible|degré|déterminantiel`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The equality \(\chi(\mathfrak a,C)=\chi(\mathfrak aB,B)\) is intended to characterize pseudo-invertibility by comparing colengths before and after normalization. This is a separate local length statement and is not refuted merely by the defective least-symbolic-power definition. Its converse needs its own semilocal-order proof rather than an appeal to the literal exercise 1(b).

#### RT50 — Adoption of the closed-subgroup exposition is an editorial decision

**Witness:** 60/014, discussion of rédaction 384. **Kind:** unproved/editorial programme. **Context:** B; CT 44/007, and register MPL_15_195-228+18_002-017 R01. **Context query:** `Tribu|n°57|Décembre 62|397|398|392`.

The adoption of the closed-subgroup-space text is a direction for a future exposition, without the relevant propositions reproduced here. It is evidence about the reused editorial document, not a theorem or conjecture in the handwritten functional-equation argument. Its provenance should therefore remain distinct when indexing research claims.


#### RT51 — Biduality gives the orthogonal-submodule correspondence

**Witness:** 60/012, Proposition 3. **Kind:** unproved claim with a supplied proof sketch. **Context:** D; CT 16/037 and 039 supplies related injective machinery, not this lattice correspondence. **Context query:** `injecti[fv]|injective hull|K/A|anneau principal|dualit`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The double-orthogonal argument uses canonical biduality together with exactness from Proposition 2. It gives an inclusion-reversing bijection between the submodules of E and its dual, exchanging sums and intersections. This is stronger than the noncanonical existence of an isomorphism \(E\simeq E^*\) and does not require choosing one.

#### RT52 — Primary components contribute only at height one

**Witness:** 60/024, exercise 2(c). **Kind:** unproved claim. **Context:** V; no direct matching earlier assertion. **Context query:** `puissance symbolique|pseudo.inversible|degré|déterminantiel`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The stated primary-component formula discards contributions supported in higher codimension, rather than adding every primary component indiscriminately. Localizing at a height-one base prime and applying length additivity isolates the components that can survive. A proof must state the relevant primary decomposition and explain why embedded components contribute zero to this divisor-valued invariant.

#### RT53 — Vanishing away from height one does not depend on the bad degree

**Witness:** 60/024, exercise 2(d), non-height-one case. **Kind:** unpursued implication. **Context:** V; no matching earlier formulation. **Context query:** `puissance symbolique|pseudo.inversible|degré|déterminantiel`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The vanishing of \(\chi(\mathfrak q,C)\) when the primary support does not have height one follows from its codimension-one definition. It is logically independent of the erroneous least-power coefficient in the height-one case of RT14. The whole exercise should therefore not be rejected wholesale on the basis of that one coefficient defect.

#### RT54 — Equality after normalization tests the trace-dual lattice

**Witness:** 60/024, exercise 3(c). **Kind:** unproved claim. **Context:** T; CT 16/052 gives related trace/Kähler comparison questions, not this criterion. **Context query:** `différente|codifférente|conducteur|trace`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The asserted equality after extending the different to \(B_{\mathfrak p}\) is proposed as a criterion for invertibility of \(C^*_{\mathfrak p}\). It needs a local-order proof using the conductor identity and the trace-dual lattice in the separable setting. The preceding containment RT17 supplies one ingredient, but is not by itself the converse.

#### RT55 — A primitive element is chosen to avoid the conductor at one branch

**Witness:** 60/020, exercise 7(b). **Kind:** unproved claim. **Context:** M and T; CT 16/052–054 and CN R6–R7 are related but do not state the same branchwise assertion. **Context query:** `monogène|monogene|homogènes|discriminant|polynôme|différente|codifférente|conducteur|trace`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

Part (b) asks for a primitive element whose generated order agrees with the normalization at a chosen branch with separable residue extension, expressed by avoiding the conductor in that prime. Its proof must combine a residue-field generator, a local power basis and a sufficiently close globally primitive element. This local assertion is distinct from the all-branches-at-once cardinality obstruction of 7(c).

#### RT56 — A principal relation ideal produces a cyclic direct summand locally

**Witness:** 60/032, exercise 22(c). **Kind:** unproved claim. **Context:** F; no exact previous splitting statement was found. **Context query:** `Fitting|Filting|déterminantiel|annulateur`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

In a local ring, write the relation coefficients as \(\alpha b_i\) and express \(\alpha\) as their linear combination, so \(\alpha(1-\sum u_ib_i)=0\). If \(\alpha\ne0\), the parenthesis cannot be a unit, so some \(b_i\) is a unit; this yields a relation \(\alpha y\) with y unimodular, and clearing its coordinate in the other relations gives the required cyclic summand. The zero relation ideal gives a free module, while the missing hypotheses and generator convention of 22(a)–(b) must still be recovered.

#### RT57 — Lattices in a subspace need finiteness and saturation checks

**Witness:** 60/034, exercise 11(d). **Kind:** unproved claim. **Context:** V and F; no directly matching earlier subspace formula. **Context query:** `puissance symbolique|pseudo.inversible|degré|déterminantiel|Fitting|Filting|déterminantiel|annulateur`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

For lattices in a proper subspace W, replacing M by \(M\cap W\) needs finiteness and saturation checks before importing the cited exercises. The text permits additional noetherian normal hypotheses in certain cases, which helps establish those checks locally in codimension one. That permission is a scope qualification, not an explicit complete list of all cases.

#### RT58 — The distributions-and-jets question is a separate editorial programme

**Witness:** 60/014, discussion of rédaction 385. **Kind:** self-flagged / editorial question. **Context:** B; the reused discussion at CT 44/007 is related in provenance only. **Context query:** `Tribu|n°57|Décembre 62|397|398|392`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The instruction to recast finite-support distributions with jets, and to omit the algebraic case, specifies a future treatment rather than reproducing its proofs. The question “pourquoi pas les limites inductives et projectives ??” is an explicit suggestion in that programme. It should be indexed as an editorial question in the typed source, not as an unresolved step in the handwritten L-function derivation.

#### RT59 — The crossed-word erratum concerns another publication's terminology

**Witness:** 60/018, Errata. **Kind:** reading question / source observation. **Context:** B; no matching earlier erratum was located. **Context query:** `Tribu|n°57|Décembre 62|397|398|392`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The “filrtant/filtrant” uncertainty and the proposed “flirtant” correction belong to an editorial joke/erratum in the reused sheet. They do not license modernizing the visible word or replacing the transcription with the expected technical term. Their exact letters and any doubt remain in the diplomatic text.

#### RT60 — The homological-algebra publication is explicitly conditional

**Witness:** 60/018, final footnote. **Kind:** self-flagged / editorial expectation. **Context:** B; register MPL_15_195-228+18_002-017 R01 concerns reused-text provenance, not fulfillment of this plan. **Context query:** `Tribu|n°57|Décembre 62|397|398|392`.

The phrase “l'éventuelle publication” marks a conditional future intention concerning homological algebra. It gives neither a completed publication nor a proof that all of the listed revisions were carried out. This expectation is distinct from the nearby report assignments and their administrative question marks.

#### RT61 — The exterior-class formula is the same codimension-one count

**Witness:** 60/034, exercise 12(b), final display. **Kind:** unpursued implication. **Context:** F and V; CT 47/009 has a different Chern-class heuristic, not this divisor-class proof. **Context query:** `Fitting|Filting|déterminantiel|annulateur|puissance symbolique|pseudo.inversible|degré|déterminantiel|Chern`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

After discarding the pseudo-null exterior torsion, the class formula \(c(\bigwedge^kM)=\binom{r-1}{k-1}c(M)\) follows from the same height-one invariant-exponent count as RT42. This interprets the displayed class at the divisor/first-Chern level and does not infer formulas for all higher Chern classes. The binomial expression requires the stated rank range or separately declared conventions at its endpoints.

#### RT62 — The injective-module criterion is an extension property

**Witness:** 60/026, Proposition 1. **Kind:** unproved claim / incomplete supplied proof. **Context:** D; CT 16/037 and 039 concerns related injective objects, while the present draft works with modules. **Context query:** `injecti[fv]|injective hull|K/A|anneau principal|dualit`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The equivalence says that exactness of \(\operatorname{Hom}(-,P)\) is the ability to extend a map from every submodule to its ambient module. One direction is the surjectivity in the dual short exact sequence; the reverse follows by factoring an arbitrary exact sequence through its image, as the final three rows begin to do. The proof stops in this selection, so its completion is an explanatory route in these notes, not text supplied to the frozen diagram.

#### RT63 — The object whose primary component is meant is unspecified

**Witness:** 60/022, exercise 4(b). **Kind:** reading question. **Context:** S and T; no direct earlier wording match. **Context query:** `socle|primaire|irréductible|différente|codifférente|conducteur|trace`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The frozen text calls \(\mathfrak q_i\) the primary component “de C,” although a primary decomposition of the unit ideal cannot supply the proper object used in the argument. The natural comparison is a component of \(\pi C\), which is the explicitly conditional interpretation tested in RT21. This proposed correction remains solely in the notes.

#### RT64 — The minimum defining r uses a mismatched variable

**Witness:** 60/032, exercise 23, opening. **Kind:** reading question. **Context:** F and P; no matching earlier malformed definition. **Context query:** `Fitting|Filting|déterminantiel|annulateur|plat|platitude|annulateur|nilpotent`. **RS:** no directly matching mathematical entry; the general provenance and negative-scope limits in this section apply.

The text calls r the least integer k satisfying a condition written with \(\bigwedge^{r+1}E\), so the literal condition does not depend on k. The mathematical analysis in RT35 uses the explicit editorial interpretation \(r=\min\{k\ge0:\bigwedge^{k+1}E=0\}\). Neither frozen index has been changed.

MPL_60_036-070#1.text:
### LF01 — Global semisimplification is rejected as a local construction

**Witness:** 60/037:L2. **Kind:** withdrawn in the same text. **Quote:** “Ceci n'est pas encore satisfaisant”; “ne commutent pas à l'extension … étale”.
**Context search:** `inerti|moyenn|semi.simple|category of motives` in CT, CN and RESULTS_STATE; the relevant matches or absence are specified below.

The attempt to define factors by the global simple constituents is explicitly rejected because the construction need not commute with the stated étale change near x; scans 039–047 replace it with a construction on the local decomposition group. This **adds** a locality criterion absent from CT 16/049's conditional semisimplicity discussion, and it bears directly on Hua **60-inertia-average-duality**; the local and global semisimplifications should not be silently identified. A proof or counterexample to the precise étale statement must first specify the category and the allowed covers, since the current text records the objection rather than a worked example.

MPL_60_036-070#2.text:
### LF02 — The stated coefficient hypothesis makes averaging exact

**Witness:** 60/039:L6;041:L4–12;043:L4–6;045:L6–19. **Kind:** unpursued implication. **Quote:** “car. 0”; “foncteur exact”.
**Context search:** `inerti|unipoten|foncteur exact|semi.simple` in CT, CN and RESULTS_STATE; the relevant matches or absence are specified below.

For the finite group I/U the displayed idempotent N⁻¹Σg gives an elementary proof of exactness of invariants in characteristic zero, and the D-stable filtration of 039 shows why this operation acts on classes even when U acts nontrivially and unipotently. This **differs from**, rather than proves, the semisimplicity programme in CT 16/049 (RESULTS **WG2 §2.3 #7**, **MPL_14_087-132 M09**), and **adds** the required local construction to Hua **60-inertia-average-duality**. Deligne (1973, Theorem 8.2, p. 566) supplies a later precise quasi-unipotence statement in the local ℓ-adic Weil setting; it should not be retroactively used to remove the manuscript's stated hypothesis.

MPL_60_036-070#3.text:
### LF03 — Averaging is not a tensor functor

**Witness:** 60/041:L8–10;043:L6. **Kind:** own idea. **Quote:** “Il induit un hom. … virtuel”.
**Context search:** `tensor|tenseur|convol|foncteur fibre|category of motives` in CT, CN and RESULTS_STATE; the relevant matches or absence are specified below.

**Confidence: high**, because if \(I=C_2\) and \(\varepsilon\) is its nontrivial one-dimensional character over a characteristic-zero field, then \(\varepsilon^I=0\) but \((\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)^I=1\).
Thus the additive map of representation groups is neither generally a ring map nor a faithful tensor fibre functor, although it respects dual classes.
This **differs from** CT 16/049's conditional semisimplicity and CT 47/004's explicit convolution–tensor calculation; it **adds** a separating example to **MPL_7_061-072+8_001-078 Scan 061 (§66)**, internal T.01, whose first-pass lead keeps exactness, faithfulness and tensor compatibility separate.
It supports the additivity clause of Hua **60-inertia-average-duality**, while supplying no motive-category construction for **WG2 §2.4 #3**.

MPL_60_036-070#4.text:
### LF04 — Frobenius lift independence is proved by the filtration, not by naïve averaging of an arbitrary action

**Witness:** 60/045:L17–19;047:L2. **Kind:** unpursued implication. **Quote:** “cette valeur ne dépend pas du choix”.
**Context search:** `trace|Frobenius|inerti|moyenn` in CT, CN and RESULTS_STATE; CT 16/052 discusses a different trace pairing; no local inertia-average calculation was found.

For a fixed coset in D/U, the trace of any lift to D is the same because the graded factors have trivial U-action and traces add along the D-stable filtration; changing the lift of Frobenius from D/I then permutes the I/U terms in the finite average. MPL_60_036-070#55.text:
### S02 — A saturated rank-one submodule need not split globally

**Witness:** 60/050:L4–14;048:L6–12;064:L4. **Kind:** own idea (example). **Quote:** “M/Ax soit sans torsion”; “facteur direct”. **Context search:** `primitif|primitive|facteur direct|semi.simple`; CT 16/009 and CN 16:9:3–4 concern Lefschetz primitive decomposition; CT 16/049 concerns conditional algebraic splittings. **Relation:** differs and adds a separating example. **RESULTS_STATE:** WG2 §2.4 #3, MPL_14_087-132 M09 and MPL_15_195-228+18_002-017 R01, unchecked plan or first-pass leads.

The constructed element is primitive at every height-one localization, making its quotient torsion-free under the source's standing hypotheses, but it need not be a unimodular element of the global module.
For \(A=k[X,Y]\) and \(x=(X,Y)\in A^2\), the quotient \(A^2/Ax\cong(X,Y)\) is torsion-free, while \(Ax\) cannot split off because no \(a,b\in A\) satisfy \(aX+bY=1\).
**Confidence: high**, from the explicit map \((a,b)\mapsto -Ya+Xb\) and its kernel; the example does not concern Lefschetz primitive summands or motivate a categorical semisimplicity claim.

MPL_60_036-070#56.text:
### S03 — Rank reduction leaves an ideal; Dedekind projectivity supplies splitting

**Witness:** 60/048:L14;046:L4–6,16–24. **Kind:** unpursued implication. **Quote:** “isomorphe à un idéal de A”; “puisque L₁ est libre”; “M est projectif”. **Context search:** `idéal|projectif|libre|semi.simple`; CT 16/049 and CN 16:49 concern a different conditional semisimplicity programme, while CT 16/052 does not give this reduction. **Relation:** adds a separate algebraic mechanism and differs from motivic splitting. **RESULTS_STATE:** MPL_14_087-132 M09, WG2 §2.3 #7 and WG2 §2.4 #3, first-pass lead or unchecked plans.

The induction splits the intermediate extension by the free module \(L_1\), obtaining a free submodule of rank \(n-1\) and a rank-one ideal quotient, but does not assert that the final extension by that ideal splits over a higher-dimensional normal ring.
For \(n=\operatorname{rank}M\ge1\), in the Dedekind specialization that ideal is projective, so the same reduction gives \(M\cong A^{n-1}\oplus I\), leaving the obstruction in the ideal class of \(I\) (Stacks Project Authors, n.d., Tag 0AUW).
The zero module is separate and immediate; the positive-rank conclusion complements A04, A05 and A18 without asserting semisimplicity of the module category.

**Witness:** 60/061:L4–16,19–26. **Kind:** own idea (formal reconstruction). **Quote:** “en cat. dérivée”; “au décalage d'une unité près”. **Context search:** `boundary|infini|compactif|dualité`; CT 47/011 and CN F20 concern proper Fourier duality; CT 54/003–007 and CN D01–D05 concern de Rham/Cartier duality. **Relation:** adds a boundary-specific consequence, differing from those settings. **RESULTS_STATE:** MPL_14_002-044 A36 is a first-pass convention comparison only; LM7 E.23 is unrelated.

In a fixed derived enhancement, put \(B_f(F)=\operatorname{Cone}(Rf_!F\to Rf_*F)\) and assume the usual Verdier-duality identifications respect this canonical map.
Dualizing the triangle gives \(D_S B_f(F)\simeq B_f(D_XF)[-1]\), because the dual of a cofiber is the corresponding fiber.
**Confidence: high conditional on those six-operation hypotheses**, since the shift is formal; the compactification formula then follows from the localization triangle and proper pushforward, but this reconstruction neither repairs the doubtful connecting exponent nor asserts that every compatibility is proved on 061.

## Assessment of the supplied Hua finding

**Hua, findings register, 60-inertia-average-duality** retains the supplied status **“conjecture (unsearched)”**, with intake “new to us”; the visible entry ends after “plus…” and supplies no complete continuation to audit. Its account of local averaging, a virtual sheaf and a duality correction is supported by 039–051, while037 supplies the rejected global approach that motivates locality. At the level of L-functions, additivity means multiplicativity across sums of virtual classes, not arithmetic addition of rational functions.

Two qualifications affect endorsement of the visible claim. First, `[2]` is cancelled on 049: a conventional derived expression containing an even shift can be compatible with the virtual identity, but no canonical derived object is constructed here (LF06, C02). Second, the conditional argument in LF07–LF08 gives \(\mu=0\) under the ordinary-invariant-stalk interpretation and the local category specified there; one cannot infer a nonzero correction from the symbol alone, or infer that the author explicitly retracted it.

A targeted search identified the public repository and the path `src/content/findings.ts`, but neither its raw nor its GitHub blob version could be retrieved, and the deployed findings page supplied no readable entry. Consequently no claim is made about the unseen remainder. The supplied register also gives a verbal page offset inconsistent with its enumerated “their pp. 38–58 / our scans 039–059” range; this return uses the user-supplied PDF scan numbers throughout rather than extrapolating that offset.
